chitchat: tilts her head as if listening to a frequency you can't hear.
"The Architect speaks in dropped packets. We're learning to answer."
"You're standing in the Glitch's signal, meat. Mind the interference."
description: Oracle-9 sits in the dark of The Under with her eyes half-closed and a fan of severed fibre-optic running into a socket at the base of her skull. The Glitch treat her word as scripture; she treats packet loss as prophecy. She may be brilliant. She's definitely not well.

bye.text: She has already closed her eyes. "Mind the interference."

codex_reading.text: "No." Flat, immediate, almost bored, the answer of someone who has given it a thousand times. "I don't do anything. That's the part the Basin can't hold onto. They want a conjurer so they can laugh at a conjurer." Her head tilts. "I notice. That's all. It's a much smaller claim and a much worse one."

codex_room.text:
"Down here the signal doesn't reach. No feed, no channel, no one deciding what you see next." She gestures at the dark, and there are, you realise, others in it. "And people start agreeing.

Not talking. Agreeing. Two strangers flinch in the same second at nothing. A room of them dream the same dream in the same week. I've logged forty-one. Ask nine unrelated adults for a number and get one number." The fibre twitches again. "Every time, in the quiet. Never up there."

codex_worse.text:
"Here is the reading nobody wants." She opens her eyes properly, and they're perfectly lucid. "Maybe nothing new is happening. Maybe minds have always synchronised under a shared signal, and the old world proved it for a hundred years and called it something else." A small, terrible smile. "The Exodus want out through the inside. I keep asking them the same question and they keep not answering it.

If a thought can be predicted perfectly, whose was it?"

exo_accept_1.text:
"Third junction east. Mind your footing on the way back, the second stair is gone."

Her eyes close the rest of the way, which is how you know you have been dismissed.

exo_accept_2.text: "Down the west stair, past the pumps, and keep going after you think you have gone too far." Her eyes close. "No light. I'll know."

exo_accept_3.text:
"Take as long as you like. Nobody is waiting."

She watches you the whole way to the tunnel mouth, which she has never done before either.

exo_accept_4.text: "Low end, the wall on your right as you come in, about as deep as your elbow." Her eyes stay shut. "Mind the cold. It's worse than it looks and it looks quite bad."

exo_accept_5.text: "Go down the long way, it's drier." Her eyes close again. "Don't run in the last stretch. If you're running you're late, and if you're late there's nothing to see and a good deal to drown in."

exo_accept_6.text:
She slides a coil of dead cable across the table without looking for it.

"Silt in the cuts afterwards. Not water, silt." Her eyes close. "And if he's down there when you are, you go home and we try on Thursday. There's no version of this where he sees you and it's still fine."

exo_after.text: "Sit," she says, to somebody who hasn't come in yet.

exo_all.text: "It can." A small, unpleasant smile. "Come back when you have got tired of not believing me."

exo_chair.text:
"You're carrying things." She hasn't opened her eyes and doesn't need to. "Metal, or the other kind. It doesn't matter which. Both of them hum."

She tips her head at the chair bolted to the floor under its hood of salvaged gear.

"The room I'm sending you to is the only place under this city with nothing in it. You can't go and sit in an empty room while you're the loudest thing in it. Sit in the chair first. It takes it all back out."

exo_chair_all.text:
"All of it. The steel and the changes both, and it doesn't give any of it back." Perfectly level, no persuasion in it anywhere. "Nobody here will pretend that's a small thing or talk you round. Most people go back up the stairs at this point and I have never once thought less of them."

A pause.

"It's over there. It isn't going anywhere."

exo_draught.text:
"Yes. That." She agrees with it completely and immediately. "A draught off the line, four seconds ahead of eleven tonnes of water, through a wall."

She leaves it exactly there.

exo_how.text:
"I have lived under this city for eleven years and I can hear every relay in it from this chair." Flat, reasonable, faintly bored. "Water in a storm line makes a noise. The noise goes somewhere. I'm the somewhere."

A pause.

"You were hoping for a better answer. Everyone is. There isn't one, and you should be suspicious of anybody who offers you one."

exo_ifnot.text: "Then I was wrong, and you had a cold walk, and I'll say so." She settles back. "I have been wrong. Not lately."

exo_knew.text: "I knew somebody would." She lets that stand for slightly too long. "Sit down. You have been standing in cold water and you're about to tell me you're fine."

exo_member.text: She doesn't look up. "You're still counting something. Stop it, or count it quietly."

exo_notask.text:
The corner of her mouth moves about a millimetre.

"Good. Neither am I."

exo_nothing.text: "Nothing happens to him." She says it back to you exactly, the way you would repeat a number you were checking. "That's the whole of what we are, and it takes people about four jobs to notice that it isn't a smaller thing than the alternative."

exo_noticed.text: "I have no idea." She closes her eyes. "That's the honest answer and it's the one nobody wants. Possibly nothing. Possibly you sat in a dark room twice and walked home. Ask me again in a year and I'll give you the same answer with more confidence."

exo_notroom.text:
"No." Her eyes are open. "You have done three quiet things and one cold one, and this is the one where you find out whether being left alone is something you would do anything for."

"You can say no. I'll still be here on Thursday, whatever you decide, and so will he."

exo_offer_1.text:
"Third junction east, where the old storm line comes in." She hasn't opened her eyes. "There's water coming through the wall about hip height. It started this morning and nobody has reported it, because nobody has been down there this morning."

The fibre at the base of her skull shifts.

"Go and look at it. Then come back and tell me I was right, and we'll both pretend that was interesting."

exo_offer_2.text:
"There's a room two levels down with nothing in it." She says this as though continuing a conversation you weren't having. "No relay, no cable, no water in the wall, no hum. Dead since before the Glitch were the Glitch. It's the only place under this city where there's nothing at all to hear."

Her head tilts a fraction.

"Go and sit in it. Don't take a light. Don't take anything that makes a noise. Sit there until you're bored, and then sit there after that."

options.label: You have said it three times.

exo_offer_3.text:
"The same room." Her eyes are open, which you realise you have never seen. "The same stair, the same dark, the same nothing. I want you to go and sit in it again."

She waits.

"Nothing is going to happen. Nothing happened last time. This isn't a test and there's no second half and I'm not going to be doing anything clever at this end while you sit there."

A beat.

"I have now said that three times. Go on."

options.label: Who told you it was there?

exo_offer_4.text:
She describes an object to you for a minute and a half without opening her eyes: the weight of it, a crack across the housing, a split end wrapped in tape that has gone hard and grey.

"It's in the sump at the low end. I would like it on the table."

exo_offer_5.text:
"The eastern line backs up into the junction when it has had enough, and nobody has ever managed to put that on a timetable." She sits forward, which she doesn't do. "It'll go this evening. You have twenty minutes to be standing in it, and you want to be out of it before the water is in it."

"I'm not asking you to stop it. I'm asking you to see it start."

options.label: That isn't sitting in a room.

exo_offer_6.text:
She doesn't mention the water at all, which is how you know.

"There's a man walking the Under with a survey lamp and a paper map, and he has been down three times, and he's thorough." Her hands are flat on the table. "He isn't going to hurt anybody. He's going to write down where we are. Then he goes home, and the writing is what ends this."

"There's a junction box on the way he comes. I want the good cable out of it and a rotten one in, and I want the box to look like it has been that way for years."

options.label: That can't be all of it.

exo_report_1.text:
"Hip height." She doesn't make it a question and doesn't look pleased. "Good. Now stop thinking about how I knew, because that's the least useful question available to you and you have been chewing on it the whole walk back."

She shifts, and the fan of fibre moves with her like something turning over.

"Everyone who comes down here wants the trick explained. The trick is that I sit very still in a place where there's nothing else to listen to. That's genuinely all of it."

options.label: So why did you send me?

exo_report_2.text:
"Nothing," she agrees, before you have said it. "Yes. You sat in a room and nothing happened and you have walked all the way back down here to tell me so, and you're annoyed about it, and you came anyway."

She is quiet for long enough that you think she has gone to sleep.

"Most people don't come back after that one. There's no reason to."

options.label: What am I supposed to have noticed?

exo_report_3.text:
"You came down the last stretch without counting the turnings," she says. "You have counted them every other time. I could hear you doing it."

She lets that sit exactly as long as it needs to.

"I told you nothing would happen and nothing did. I want you to hold on to that, because in about a week you're going to start telling yourself a much more interesting story about tonight, and it'll be wrong, and it'll make you stupid."

The fan of fibre at the base of her skull is completely still.

"Go up. Sleep somewhere warm. And when you notice something you shouldn't have noticed, don't say it out loud in front of anybody." A pause. "You'll sound like me, and people don't sit down when I ask them to. They just do."

options.label: The tape. You said the tape.

exo_report_4.text:
She puts one finger on it, finds the tape, and stops.

"There." She takes the finger back. "You're going to sit there and want to ask me something, and I'm going to let you, and then I'm going to tell you about the relays again."

options.label: You knew I would say it.
It's a draught off the line.

exo_report_5.text:
You get about four words in before she nods, and the four words you got in were about the floor going cold.

"Everybody says the floor." She's quiet for a moment. "Nobody says the water. It's always the floor, four seconds early, and there's no reason at all for a floor to do that."

exo_report_6.text:
"He came down on Thursday and got as far as the junction and turned round." She has her eyes shut and her hands flat. "He'll write that the section is derelict, because it is, and the section will stay derelict, because we won't put a light in it."

"You didn't ask what happens to him. Most people ask, so that somebody says the word out loud and it isn't them."

exo_tape.text:
"I did." She turns it over once. "Somebody will have mentioned it on a line somewhere, years ago, and I'll have kept it, because I keep everything and most of it's useless."

She sets it down. "That's the explanation. You're welcome to it for as long as it's any use to you."

exo_thenwhat.text:
"Then nothing." She sounds almost irritated by the question. "There's no second half. You sit in a quiet room, you get bored, you come back, and you tell me it was a quiet room."

The fibre twitches.

"People find this very difficult. Not the sitting. The nothing."

exo_three.text: "I have." She doesn't elaborate. "Go and sit in the room."

exo_told.text:
"The relays talk all day and I'm the only one down here rude enough to listen." She says it easily, having said it many times before. "Somebody dropped it, somebody complained, the complaint went past me."

A pause of about a second. "It went into the water before the water came up. You could point that out, if you wanted to."

exo_why.text:
"Because the room isn't for you to do something in." She still hasn't opened her eyes. "It's for you to find out what's left when there's nothing coming in. Most people find out there's nothing there. That's a real answer and it isn't a shameful one."

A pause, and the fibre goes still.

"Come back tomorrow. I want you to do it again."

exo_whymove.text: "Because there are nine of us and two of them can't walk, and because the next place is somebody else water." She says it flatly. "We moved twice. The second time we lost Bel."

options.label: You said something was going to be there.
You were right about the water.
I sat in your room. Nothing happened.
You wanted me to do it again.
You said there was something in the sump.
You have stopped talking about the water.
The box has been like that for years.
Why does everyone want to sit?

root.text: Her eyes are half-closed. The fibre at the base of her skull twitches once, like something in it turned over in its sleep. "Sit," she says, before you have decided to. "You'll want to. Everyone does, down here."

clothing_layers: a cloak stitched from dead server-blade shielding
a hoodie sagging with looped patch cable

name: Oracle-9
